claims.text: Integrating DFT with phonon-scattering models that explicitly represent configurational disorder will improve the accuracy of lattice thermal-conductivity predictions for high-entropy alloys.
FeCoCrMnNi is a configurationally disordered random alloy.
The targeted HEAs are single-phase and equiatomic or near-equiatomic.
The proposed method couples ab initio DFT with many-body phonon-scattering calculations that explicitly incorporate disorder-induced force-constant fluctuations.
Phonon scattering dominates thermal transport in crystalline HEAs between approximately 300 and 700 K.
Atomic-scale configurational disorder produces force-constant fluctuations.
Force-constant fluctuations increase acoustic-phonon scattering or attenuation in FeCoCrMnNi.
Lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys can reduce phonon velocity and enhance phonon scattering.
Mass variations enhance phonon scattering in the targeted HEAs.
Enhanced disorder-induced phonon scattering reduces phonon lifetimes.
Lattice-distortion-induced phonon scattering leads to low lattice thermal conductivity.
Explicitly modeling configurational disorder will produce more accurate acoustic-phonon dispersions.
The integrated method will predict lower lattice thermal conductivity than conventional DFT or MD models.
The integrated method will reduce relative error in lattice thermal-conductivity estimates by roughly 20% compared with current computational approaches.
The integrated method will reliably identify HEA compositions with low lattice thermal conductivity.
Conventional DFT and MD have limitations in representing important HEA disorder phenomena.
Those limitations cause inaccuracies in conventional thermal-conductivity predictions.
The proposed approach is applicable primarily to HEAs with simple crystalline structures.
The approach may not be reliable for alloys with extremely high chemical complexity, significant secondary phases, or amorphous regions.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement of approximately 20% in relative prediction error versus a conventional model would falsify the hypothesis.
